published_figures.source: DoD Selected Acquisition Report, F-22, December 2010; USAF F-22 fact sheet
published_figures.figure: The report's supercruise, "Vmax/Opt Alt/Mil Power": Mach 1.76, demonstrated, at military power, 0.99, and the best altitude - flown level at every 2,000 ft from 30,000 to 50,000 ft, the fastest.
The report's acceleration, "Acceleration/.8-1.5/30K": 52.4 seconds, demonstrated, from Mach 0.8 to 1.5 at 30,000 ft, at maximum power.

The report's manoeuvrability, "max power sustained G", at 30,000 ft and Mach 0.9: 3.7 g, demonstrated - a turn rate of 7.34 degrees a second, g times the root of n squared less one, over the true airspeed, 895 ft/s. The tolerance takes in the report's objective, 3.9 g.

The fact sheet's speed, "mach two class": level at 40,000 ft at full throttle it reaches Mach 2, within the class this project reads as 1.95 to 2.35. Lockheed Martin (18 November 2002) had it cleared to Mach 2.
The fact sheet's ceiling, "above 50,000 feet": at 50,000 ft, at maximum power, it still climbs at 100 ft/min, the rate that makes a service ceiling.

**Measured, not published** (the owner's decision of 2026-10-09): her flight manual, T.O. 1F-22A-1, is not public, and no stall or approach speed for her was found (searched 2026-10-09, 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02). This is 14 CFR 1.2's VS0, "the stalling speed or the minimum steady flight speed in the landing configuration", measured from her model: trimmed level at 1 g, gear down and no flap, at 5,000 ft, from the entry speed down until no trim holds, where her stabilators reach their stop at 27.5 degrees of alpha (src/sim/figures.cpp, `steady_flight_speed`). The deceleration the other stalls here are measured by does not hold still on her rate-command stick (131 to 149 KCAS by its entry speed alone). From 160, 200 and 240 KCAS it is 90.0 within a tenth. What it asserts is that the model still does what it did, not that the aeroplane does it. Her approach speed is 1.3 times it, as every aircraft's here: 123.8 kt at her model's own 61,570 lb, flown on the centreline in calm air and 15 kt across and touched within 360 ft/min on her power (docs/status/2026-11-02-the-f22a-s-flare-flown-on-her-power.md).
published_figures.plan_speeds: The slowest, 140 kt, is 5 kt over the first that held, 135: she then published no stall speed, so had no approach speed, and the sweep began at 120 kt - under her approach speed now, 123.8 kt at this weight (1.3 times her measured slowest steady flight, 2026-11-02); below 135 she came down 500 ft before reaching her circle. At 135 she held the orbit all four ways and, on her own yaw damper and rudder integral (her catalogue's `yaw-damper`), her sideslip in the crosswind within 0.23 degree. On 2026-10-02, before them, she held her orbit only from 220 kt and swung her sideslip 6.0 degrees either way at 230 in the crosswind, and her slowest was 255. The fastest, 360 kt, a fifth over its start speed, held all four ways.
published_figures.glide_speeds: 225 kt asserted; 140 to 220 observed departing past 89 degrees of alpha before a third of the way round. At 225 she goes round both ways at 8.1 degrees at most. Her climb speed, 220, is below it, so 225 is the one speed a glide may ask of her. Before 2026-10-10 the trial flew her with her gear down, and she glided at no speed from 140 to 335 kt.
published_figures.takeoff_speeds: Rotation: from 100 kt in 5 kt steps, the first that lifted her off within 15 kt of itself, unwrecked, inside the 3,500 m runway, and never 5 kt slower once off, was 145 kt, unstuck (5 ft up) at 156 kt; 150 is written, 5 kt to spare, and she is unstuck at about 158 - against the Fallon report's 143 and 164. Rotated sooner, her nose comes up at four degrees a second and she floats in ground effect: rotated at 110 she was unstuck only at 143, and at 140 at 155, just over 15 kt on. Until 2026-10-14 110 was written: her pitch loop's integrator, wound up against her nose wheel, snatched her nose up at ten to thirteen degrees a second and threw her off at about 119. The climb away: asked 120 to 205 kt, at military power she was at 500 ft never slower than 222.7 kt, and faster the faster asked - she cannot be held slower - which is written rounded up. With no flap, at 61,570 lb, the weight her model flies a plan at.
published_figures.landing_distance: Measured, not published: the line above is written by tools/measured_landing.py from `glideslope_cli land f22` (2026-11-02, linux-release). Landed by the approach autopilot from a final-approach gate 2 nm out, on a level runway at sea level in calm air with every tank full (63,960 lb), at 1.3 times her measured slowest steady flight for that weight, she touched 416 m in at 157 ft/min, her nose 14.3 degrees up, and stopped 1,861 m past the threshold, which she crossed on the 3-degree glidepath. The figure is that, 2 per cent over and rounded up to 100 ft (3 per cent over in all), for the drift between machines: the AI's own landing in those conditions, not a regulatory distance and not a minimum; heavier, hotter, higher or downwind she needs more, and nothing here allows for it. Factor 1, as it is the landing a plan flies, not a demonstrated minimum to be given a margin. **No landing distance is published for her**: searched 2026-10-09, the USAF fact sheet and the Selected Acquisition Report give none, and the 3,000 ft quoted elsewhere is the Advanced Tactical Fighter's design requirement as retold by secondary sources, not a flight manual figure; searched again 2026-10-13, AFMAN 11-2F-22A volume 1 (12 April 2019, as attached to solicitation FA5000-21-R-0002) gives none, and her flight manual, T.O. 1F-22A-1, is not published; again 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02, nothing found. Until 2026-11-02 she had no approach speed, so this could not be measured and every landing was refused her.
published_figures.no_cg_limits: Her weight and centre-of-gravity envelope is not published: her flight manual is not public, and no Air Force, NASA or academic source found (2026-10-24) gives her limits.
